newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols firm as market climbs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols firm as market climbs.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. index options remained well bid Tuesday as the market posted solid gains, traders said.
"They're looking for something. I don't know what it is," one S&P 500 index options trader said, referring to investors who kept options premiums pumped up
By about 1130 CDT/1630 GMT, the Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index was up 0.44, or about 1.9 percent, at 23.78, off its 24.36 session high.
"Over 24 I think the VIX is probably at an all-time premium high relative to the crash of '87," the trader said.
The VIX is calculated off certain S&P 100 index options. The OEX was up 5.54 at 866.69 after hitting 869.95.
The spot SPX was ahead 5.72 at 890.86 and September S&P 500 futures added 8.25 to 898.50.
September futures reached 903.25 before easing back.
"We've put together a good rally finally," said one S&P 500 futures-options trader. "Good rally, good volume. They tried a couple of times to break it but it's held its own."
He said some investors had put on strangles in the August series "basically playing to the long side."
Volatilities in S&P 500 futures-options were also holding firm, he said, adding that caution was creeping into the market.
"We'll probably see a pullback (off the day's highs) because of nervousness coming through with this Fed meeting over our heads," the trader said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rate policy, is meeting today and Wednesday, but few expect a change in rates.
The SPX options trader said he expected the VIX to hold firm through Wednesday into Thursday morning, when the government releases key employment data for June.
"I think they're going to beat it up Thursday," he said, referring to the volatility index.
At the very least, more time erosion will be seen than normal Thursday, because the market closes early for a three-day holiday weekend.
The market will be closed Friday in observance of Independence Day.
